info.title: noobly Wiki — Document API
info.description:
Read-oriented document API for the noobly Wiki Platform (port 9101).

This spec is intentionally scoped to the **document operations** an external consumer (e.g. an MCP server) needs to read knowledge out of the wiki:

- **Spaces** — list the available knowledge spaces and read a single space.
- **Browse** — walk a space's folder/document tree, or list a single directory.
- **Documents** — fetch a document's content (text as JSON, binary as raw bytes) or download the raw file.
- **Search** — full-text search to discover documents to read.

The tool-management surface (workflows, executions, schedules, connections, agents, settings, RBAC, social/notifications, onboarding, blueprint, datasources content, etc.) is intentionally **excluded**. The complete platform API is preserved alongside this file as `openapi.full.json`.

**Identity model:** documents are addressed by `spaceId` (integer) + `path` (relative to the space root, using `/` separators). Call `GET /applications/wiki/api/spaces` first to map a space name to its `spaceId`, then browse the tree to discover paths, then read content by path.

BearerAuth.description: Bearer token (e.g. a personal `dtk_` API token). Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. This is the recommended scheme for programmatic / MCP access. Public spaces are readable without any credential; team and private spaces require a token whose user has access.

SessionAuth.name: connect.sid
SessionAuth.description: Session cookie issued after an interactive login. Mainly used by the browser UI; programmatic consumers should prefer BearerAuth.

code.description: Underlying error code where available, e.g. ENOENT, EACCES

Space.description: A knowledge space (a top-level container of folders and documents).

id.description: Numeric space identifier — use this as `spaceId` in the browse and document endpoints

name.description: Human-readable space name (also returned as `spaceName` on document nodes and search results)

visibility.description: public = readable by anyone; team = readable by authenticated users; private = readable only by users in allowedUsers

TreeNode.description:
A node in a space's folder tree. Folders carry `children`; documents are leaves addressed by `path`.

The wire format is LEAN: `path`, `title`, `fileName` and `spaceName` are omitted because a client can derive them (`path` = parent path + '/' + `name`; the rest are copies of `name` or constant for the response). `status` is omitted when unset rather than sent as null.

path.description: Path relative to the space root (use this as `documentPath` when reading content). OMITTED on the wire — rebuild it from the nesting.

title.description: Present on document nodes. OMITTED on the wire — equals `name` (or the space being requested).

fileName.description: Present on document nodes. OMITTED on the wire — equals `name` (or the space being requested).

spaceName.description: Present on document nodes. OMITTED on the wire — equals `name` (or the space being requested).

status.description: Optional navigation accent / status colour; omitted when unset

truncated.description: Folder nodes only. `true` means the walk stopped here and this folder has NOT been listed — `children` is empty because nothing was read, not because the folder is empty. Re-request with `path` set to this folder to list it.

path.description: The folder this tree is rooted at ('' = space root); echoes the `path` query parameter.

files.description: Entries in the directory. Depending on the space's filing provider, each entry is either a bare file/folder name or an object with name + type metadata.

FileContent.description: Text/markdown document content. Returned for textual viewer types (markdown, code, text, web, data). Office documents (docx/xlsx/pptx) are returned as their derived markdown sidecar with `metadata.derivedFrom` set. Binary files are NOT returned via this schema — they are streamed as raw bytes (see the binary response content types).

content.description: The document text. Empty string for download-only file types.

provider.description: Filing provider backing the space (e.g. local, ftp, s3)

viewer.description: How the platform renders this file. 'download' means a binary/unsupported file with no inline text.

derivedFrom.description: Set when content is the markdown sidecar derived from an office original at this path

ChangeEvent.description: A single file or folder change recorded by the platform's file watcher / API. Emitted in chronological order (oldest first). Consumers persist the feed's `cursor` and pass it back as `since` to receive only newer events.

timestamp.description: When the change was recorded (ISO 8601). The most recent event's timestamp is echoed as the feed `cursor`.

space.description: The space the changed item belongs to

id.description: Space id — matches the `since`/`spaceId` filter and the id used elsewhere in this API

item.description: The changed file or folder. `path` is relative to the space root using `/` separators, so it can be fed directly to the document/browse endpoints.

path.description: Path relative to the space root

oldPath.description: Present on rename/move — the previous path

newPath.description: Present on rename/move — the new path

oldParentPath.description: Present on move — the previous parent path

userId.description: Present when the change came from an authenticated API action

userName.description: Present when the change came from an authenticated API action

ChangesFeed.description: A page of change events plus the cursor to continue from.

events.description: Matching events in chronological order (oldest first).

cursor.description: Timestamp of the newest event returned (or of the newest event on record when this page is empty). Persist it and send it as `since` on the next poll. Null when the feed is empty.

truncated.description: True when your `since` cursor is older than the oldest event still retained in memory — some changes were missed, so perform a full sync (browse + folder-tree) and reset your cursor from `serverTime`.

serverTime.description: Server clock at response time. Use as the initial cursor for a first-time / post-truncation full sync.

tags.name: Browse
tags.description: Walk a space's folder/document tree or list a single directory

tags.name: Documents
tags.description: Read document content (text or binary) and download raw files

tags.name: Changes
tags.description: Poll a cursor-based feed of file/folder changes to consume only what changed since your last sync

get.description: Returns the spaces the caller can see. Use the returned `id` as `spaceId` in the browse and document endpoints, and `name` to correlate with `spaceName` on tree nodes and search results.

get.summary: Get a space's folder/document tree (lazy, depth-limited)
get.description:
Returns a nested tree of folders and documents in a space. Hidden files (those beginning with `.`) are omitted. Supports ETag / `If-None-Match` for cheap revalidation (304 when unchanged).

**The walk is depth-limited.** By default only 2 levels are listed; a folder below the cut is returned with `children: []` and `truncated: true`, which means **not listed yet** — not empty. Fetch it by repeating the request with `path` set to that folder. Pass `depth=all` for the full recursive tree; on a large content root that request can take minutes, which is why it is opt-in.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Previously returned ETag; yields 304 when the tree is unchanged

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Space-relative folder to return the subtree of. Omit (or '' / '/') for the space root. Returns 404 if the space's allowedPaths/excludedPaths hide it, 400 on a traversal attempt.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Levels to list below `path`. `all` (or `0`) walks everything, still capped by WIKI_TREE_MAX_DEPTH. Defaults to WIKI_TREE_DEPTH (2).

404.description: Space not found, or `path` is hidden by the space's path filter

get.summary: List the contents of a single directory
get.description: Lists the immediate entries of one directory within a space (non-recursive). Pass an empty `directoryPath` (or `.`) for the space root. For a full recursive view use the folder-tree endpoint instead.

parameters.name: directoryPath
parameters.description: Directory path relative to the space root (may contain `/`). Use `.` for the root.

get.summary: Get document content (text as JSON, binary as raw bytes)
get.description:
Reads a document by path within a space.

- **Text documents** (markdown, code, plain text, web, data) return `application/json` matching the `FileContent` schema, with the text in `content`.
- **Office documents** (docx/xlsx/pptx) return their derived markdown sidecar as `FileContent` (with `metadata.derivedFrom`). When no sidecar exists yet, an empty `content` with `metadata.viewer = 'download'` is returned — fetch the original via the download endpoint.
- **Binary documents** (image, pdf, video, audio) are streamed as raw bytes with the appropriate `Content-Type` (not JSON-wrapped).

parameters.name: documentPath
parameters.description: Document path relative to the space root (may contain `/`).

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: Read encoding for text responses. Ignored for binary viewer types (always raw bytes).

200.description: Document content. Media type depends on the file: JSON for text/markdown, raw bytes for binary.

get.summary: Download the raw file (binary or text)
get.description: Streams the unmodified file content as raw bytes with the MIME type derived from its extension. Unlike the file-content endpoint, this always returns the original bytes (never a derived markdown sidecar), making it the correct choice for downloading office documents, images, PDFs and any binary asset. Set `?download=true` to receive a `Content-Disposition: attachment` header.

parameters.name: documentPath
parameters.description: Document path relative to the space root (may contain `/`).

get.description: Searches indexed document content and titles. Spaces are filtered by id (consistent with the rest of this API) — pass `spaceId` for a single space or `spaceIds` for several. Each result carries both `spaceId` and `spaceName` plus the document `path`, so a result can be read directly via the document endpoints.

parameters.name: spaceId
parameters.description: Restrict to a single space (by id)

parameters.name: spaceIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of space ids to restrict to

parameters.name: fileTypes
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of file types/extensions to restrict to

parameters.name: includeContent
parameters.description: Include a content excerpt/body with each result

path.description: Document path relative to its space root

get.summary: Poll the change feed for incremental sync
get.description:
Returns file/folder change events so a client can consume **only what changed** since its last poll instead of re-crawling every document. This is the endpoint the wiki sync daemon uses.

**How to use it:**
1. First call **without** `since` — you get the full retained event ring plus a `cursor` (and `serverTime`). For a fresh client, discard the events and seed your cursor from `serverTime`, then do a one-time full crawl (folder-tree + file-content).
2. On each subsequent poll, pass the previously returned `cursor` as `since`. You receive only events strictly newer than that timestamp, and a fresh `cursor` to store.
3. If the response has `truncated: true`, your cursor fell off the back of the in-memory ring (you polled too infrequently) — discard the partial events, run a full sync, and reset your cursor from `serverTime`.

Events are returned oldest-first. `cursor` is the timestamp of the newest event (so it is safe to reuse even when `events` is empty).

**Auth:** unlike the public read endpoints, this feed always requires an authenticated caller (bearer token or session) — it spans all spaces the caller can see unless narrowed with `spaceId`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp (normally the `cursor` from your previous call). Only events strictly after this time are returned. Omit for the first call to receive the full retained ring.

parameters.name: spaceId
parameters.description: Restrict the feed to a single space id.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of events to return (default 500, capped at 1000). When more than `limit` events match, the newest `limit` are returned.

200.description: A page of change events with a continuation cursor.

503.description: Change feed unavailable (event bus not initialized)
